facts.statement: The genus Protohadros was described by Head in 1998.
facts.quote: authority: Head, 1998

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Protohadros is Protohadros byrdi.
facts.quote: type_species: Protohadros byrdi

facts.statement: Protohadros lived approximately 100 to 93.9 million years ago during the early Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: approximately 100-93.9 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Protohadros have been found in what is now Texas, United States.
facts.quote: of what is now Texas, United States

facts.statement: Remains of Protohadros, including ribs and an ungual, were discovered by Gary Byrd in early 1994.
facts.quote: Gary Byrd, a part-time palaeontologist, discovered some remains of this euornithopod (ribs and an ungual) during early 1994

facts.statement: The remains were found at Flower Mound in Denton County, north-central Texas.
facts.quote: at Flower Mound, Denton County, north-central Texas

facts.statement: Protohadros was first reported in 1996 by Jason Head.
facts.quote: It was first reported upon in 1996 by Jason Head

facts.statement: The species Protohadros byrdi was formally described and named by Head in 1998.
facts.quote: The type species Protohadros byrdi was described and named by Head in 1998

facts.statement: The specific name 'byrdi' honors the discoverer Gary Byrd.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Byrd

facts.statement: The holotype specimen SMU 74582 was recovered from the Woodbine Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, specimen SMU 74582, of Protohadros, was found in the Woodbine Formation

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skull, rib fragments, a hand ungual, and a neural arch.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skull, pieces of ribs, a hand ungual and a neural arch

facts.statement: In 1997, Yuong-Nam Lee named possible Protohadros tracks as the ichnospecies Caririchnium protohadrosaurichnos.
facts.quote: In 1997 Lee named possible tracks of Protohadros as the ichnospecies Caririchnium protohadrosaurichnos

facts.statement: Its total body length is estimated to be in the range of 6 to 8 meters.
facts.quote: and a total body length likely in the range of 6–8 meters

facts.statement: The premaxilla forms a broad, expanded beak.
facts.quote: The premaxilla forms a broad, expanded beak

facts.statement: The beak lacks teeth but features a slightly textured surface along the oral margin.
facts.quote: It lacks teeth, as in other hadrosaurs, and shows a slightly rugose (textured) surface along the oral margin

facts.statement: The maxilla houses a dental battery with approximately 36 tooth positions.
facts.quote: It houses a dental battery with about 36 tooth positions

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the downward muzzle shape indicates Protohadros specialized in low-growing plants.
facts.quote: the downward muzzle shape indicates that Protohadros was likely specializing in low-growing plants

facts.statement: Its diet likely consisted of vegetation found in floodplains or deltaic zones.
facts.quote: probably in floodplains or deltaic vegetation zones

facts.statement: Protohadros may have also consumed aquatic vegetation.
facts.quote: It could have also eaten aquatic vegetation

facts.statement: The discovery of Protohadros sparked a debate regarding whether hadrosaurids originated in Asia or North America.
facts.quote: Before Protohadros, many researchers leaned toward an Asian origin for hadrosaurids. But the presence of such an early and basal form in North America suggested that a North American origin was just as plausible, if not equally supported

facts.statement: The genus name references Head's view that this species was the oldest known hadrosaur.
facts.quote: Head considered the species the oldest known hadrosaur
